newsitem.title: USA: GM talks continue in Oklahoma plant strike.
newsitem.headline: GM talks continue in Oklahoma plant strike.

text.p: A strike by United Auto Workers union workers at a key General Motors Corp car plant entered its third day Monday, with bargainers still trying to hammer out a new contract for about 3,500 workers.

Members of UAW Local 1999 in Oklahoma City, Okla., walked off the job early Saturday morning, after contract disagreements over staffing and health and safety issues failed to avert a strike at the plant.

GM spokesman Chuck Licari said talks resumed Monday morning after adjourning late Sunday afternoon. Local 1999 Vice President Yvonne Smith said union members on the picket lines remain committed to the walkout.
"The general consensus of our membership is we have to do whatever is necessary to resolve our problem, and if that means withholding our labor, that's what we're prepared to do," she said.

The walkout prevented GM from resuming production of its new Chevrolet Malibu and Oldsmobile Cutlass cars at the plant, which is GM's main production source for the cars. The redesigned cars, priced at about $16,000 to $18,000, are a cornerstone of GM's efforts to regain market share in the hotly contested U.S. intermediate car segment.

To become more competitive, GM is trying to lower its hourly workforce through attrition and efficiency gains. At the Oklahoma City plant, GM says it needs 900 fewer workers to build the new Malibu and Cutlass versions.
But the union, whose members say they are overworked with growing numbers of injuries, wants GM to replace 500 workers lost to retirements and transfers to other plants in recent months.
